deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page, items 1-5): this is a lecture write-up ('Vortrag des Newtonschen Lehrsatzes'). The equation is x^m + P x^{m-1} + Q x^{m-2} + ... + U = 0 with roots α, β, γ, δ, .... Reversing it gives Z(t) := 1 + P t + Q t^2 + R t^3 + ... + U t^m = ∏(1 - α t) (item 3).

Item 4 is the divided-difference identity Z(t) - Z(u) = (t-u)[P + Q(t+u) + R(t^2+tu+u^2) + ... + U(t^{m-1} + t^{m-2}u + ... + u^{m-1})]. It follows from t^k - u^k = (t-u)(t^{k-1} + ... + u^{k-1}).

Item 5 telescopes the product. With roots α_1..α_m:
∏(1-α_i t) - ∏(1-α_i u) = Σ_k [∏_{i<k}(1-α_i u)]·[(1-α_k t) - (1-α_k u)]·[∏_{i>k}(1-α_i t)].
The middle factor equals (u-t) α_k.

Item 6 (this page): divide both expressions for the difference by (t-u). Since (u-t)/(t-u) = -1:
P + Q(t+u) + R(t^2+tu+u^2) + ... + V(t^{m-1} + ... + u^{m-1}) = -α(1-βt)(1-γt)(1-δt)... - β(1-αu)(1-γt)(1-δt)... - γ(1-αu)(1-βu)(1-δt)... - δ(1-αu)(1-βu)(1-γu)... - ...
Here the last coefficient is called V; on the previous page it was U.

Item 7: set u = t. The left side becomes the derivative Z'(t) = P + 2Qt + 3Rt^2 + ... + m V t^{m-1}. Each product on the right becomes Z/(1-α_k t). Hence
Z'(t) + Σ_k α_k Z/(1-α_k t) = 0.
In effect this is the logarithmic derivative Z'/Z = -Σ α_k/(1-α_k t), obtained without logarithms by a finite-difference/limit argument.

Item 8: substitute Z = 1 + Pt + Qt^2 + ... and expand 1/(1-αt) = Σ α^j t^j (geometric series, 'by division'). This gives
αZ/(1-αt) = α + (α^2 + αP) t + (α^3 + α^2 P + αQ) t^2 + (α^4 + α^3 P + α^2 Q + αR) t^3 + ...,
and likewise for the other roots.

Item 9: sum over the roots, with S_k = α^k + β^k + γ^k + ... the power sums:
Σ α_k Z/(1-α_k t) = S_1 + (S_2 + P S_1) t + (S_3 + P S_2 + Q S_1) t^2 + (S_4 + P S_3 + Q S_2 + R S_1) t^3 + ...

Item 10: add Z'(t) and set every coefficient of t to zero:
- S_1 + P = 0
- S_2 + P S_1 + 2Q = 0
- S_3 + P S_2 + Q S_1 + 3R = 0
- etc.
These are Newton's identities ('welches das Newtonsche Theorem ist'), as the page says.

Implicit (mine, not on the page): for k > m the term k·(coefficient) vanishes, giving S_k + P S_{k-1} + ... + U S_{k-m} = 0.

The upside-down words at right are unrelated pen trials. The next page turns to the lemma |Ω| < |a| for the fundamental theorem of algebra, citing Drobisch 1834, so this is late teaching material.
errors: Item 7: the last term of the derivative is written 'mV'; it should be m V t^{m-1}. It is harmless here because only the coefficients of t^0, t^1, t^2 are used, but as written the identity is wrong for m > 1.
Notation slip: the last coefficient is U on the previous page (items 1, 3, 4) but V on this page (items 6, 7).
Item 10: the struck-out first attempts ('P+S_1=0', 'Q+') show the writer self-correcting. The final equations are correct.
The general continuation S_k + P S_{k-1} + ... + kK = 0 for k ≤ m, and S_k + ... + U S_{k-m} = 0 for k > m, is left as '&c.' without stating the change at k > m. This is a gap, not an error.

results.what: Telescoping/divided-difference identity for a product of linear factors; letting u→t gives Z'(t) = -Σ α Z/(1-αt) without logarithms.
results.modern_name: Logarithmic derivative of a polynomial via a difference quotient (product rule)

results.what: Expansion αZ/(1-αt) = Σ_n (α^{n+1} + Pα^n + Qα^{n-1} + ...) t^n and its sum over the roots, expressed through the power sums S_k.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a lecture-style proof of Newton's identities by a standard generating-function/logarithmic-derivative argument, explicitly attributed on the page to Newton. Nothing here is new or non-standard; it is didactic material.
